model_annotation: The chart is a grouped bar chart illustrating an “effect” measure across language-family categories for six model/condition combinations indicated in the legend. The horizontal axis contains the categorical groups (left to right): IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear numeric scale with major tick labels shown at approximately 0, 10, 20, and 30 (with values extending slightly below 0 and up to the mid-30s). For each category, six side-by-side bars are shown in a consistent left-to-right order and color scheme matching the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (pink), and XLM-B₂ (red); each bar includes a vertical error bar with capped whiskers. Approximate bar heights by group are: IE-Baltic shows small positive values (light/dark blue around ~1–2, light/dark green around ~3–4, pink/red around ~5–6); IE-Germanic shows light/dark blue near ~9–10, light green near ~1 and dark green slightly below 0, and pink/red near ~15; IE-Indic shows light/dark blue near 0 (slightly above or below), light/dark green around ~18–20, pink around ~23–24, and red around ~20–21; IE-Romance shows light/dark blue around ~5–6, light green around ~5, dark green near ~1, pink around ~12, and red around ~5–6; IE-Slavic family shows light/dark blue around ~9–10, light/dark green near ~0–1, pink around ~17, and red around ~15–16; IE-other shows light/dark blue around ~6, light/dark green near ~0, and pink/red around ~8; Isolate shows all bars close to 0 with small positives (greens and pink/red roughly ~1–2) and blues approximately at 0; Semitic shows light blue around ~11, dark blue around ~16, light green slightly below 0, dark green near 0, pink around ~15, and red around ~19–20; and Uralic shows values clustered near 0–2 with the pink bar around ~2 and other bars near ~0.5–1. The category order appears fixed by the listed family names rather than sorted by bar height, and no bars are uniquely highlighted beyond the standard color coding and the presence of error bars.
